marks.gloss_en: וליגזר נמי על מיעוטו שאינו מקפיד משום מיעוטו המקפיד, אי נמי משום רובו שאינו מקפיד!
היא גופא גזירה, ואנן ניקום ונגזר גזירה לגזירה?! (= p_gezera_ligzera)
it is itself a decree; shall we arise and decree a decree for a decree?
מחיצין -- הא דאמרן. הניחא לרבי יהודה, אלא לרבי מאיר מאי איכא למימר? -- for R' Meir the ten is derived from verses (5b.9-11)
כי אתאי הלכתא -- לגוד, ולבוד, ודופן עקומה (= p_hlmm_gud_lavud, aliba R' Meir)
when the halakha came, it was for gud, lavud and the bent wall
R' Yitzchak: by Torah law, [an interposition over] most of him that he is particular about interposes
two walls according to their law, and the third even a handbreadth
in what do they disagree? the Rabbis hold the written form is authoritative; R' Shimon holds the read form is authoritative
[as written] בסכת, בסכת, בסכות -- here are four
take away one for [the mitzva] itself, three remain: two according to their law [and a third]
[as read] בסכות, בסכות, בסכות -- here are six
or say: all agree the read form is authoritative, and they disagree over this -- one master holds its covering requires a verse, the other that it does not
or say: all agree the written form is authoritative, and they disagree over this -- one master holds the halakha comes to reduce, the other that it comes to add

or say: all agree the halakha comes to reduce and the written form is authoritative, and they disagree over whether first occurrences are expounded -- one master holds they are, the other that they are not (the text does not say which master is which)
R' Shimon's reason is from here: 'and there shall be a sukkah for shade by day from the heat, and for refuge and cover from storm and from rain' (Yeshayahu 4:6)
where does he set that handbreadth? Rav: he sets it opposite the one that projects
